# GEO report: trailhead

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 55–64/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 19 of 21 points).
How it's calculated: low = 11.5 ÷ 21 × 100 = 55. High = (11.5 + 2) ÷ 21 × 100 = 64.

All results are read from code, not measured on a live site. The biggest losses are that pages are built only in the browser, the sitemap pointer in `robots.txt` isn't a full URL, and the home page reaches the guides page only through a button. One rule is unknown because the site's real domain isn't declared.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Make pages render on the server
- **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends and don't run JavaScript. With browser-only rendering, they may see an empty page.
- **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2`
- **What the code says:** `ssr: false,`
- **Size:** Medium
- **Score after this:** 69–79

### 2. Make the `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt a full URL
- **Why it matters:** The `Sitemap:` line must be an absolute URL, or crawlers may not find your page list.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4`
- **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 64–74

### 3. Link to the guides page with a real link
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers follow `<a href>` links. A button that runs script isn't a link, so the guides page has no crawlable path from the home page.
- **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8`
- **What the code says:** `<button @click="router.push('/guides')">Trail guides</button>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 64–74

Each "score after" is for that fix alone. They add up if you do several.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Clear | Not run | Only `/admin` is disallowed (`robots.txt:2`). I assumed you want to be found, since there's no config. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/guides` is noindexed by `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`. `/` is clear, so 1 of 2 routes. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical link | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical anywhere (`app.vue:2` sets only a title). The real domain isn't declared, so I need it from you. |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2`, site-wide |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the project |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap found and valid | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4` is relative. The sitemap itself is valid. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `lang` is set (`nuxt.config.ts:5`). `/guides` inherits the home title and description (`app.vue:2`, `nuxt.config.ts:6`), so 1 of 2 routes is clear. |
| GEO-016 | Server-rendered links to key pages | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`, 0 of 1 route |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits vs AI-search policy | Clear | Not run | The middleware sets only `noindex`, and there's no `nosnippet` |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Not run | I read all three pages and `app.vue`. They have no images, and the button has text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present; not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app |

## Other problems found

- **A sitemap page is noindexed by a header.** `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `<loc>https://trailhead.example/guides</loc>`, but `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` sets `X-Robots-Tag` to `noindex` for it. Remove that header, or drop the page from the sitemap if it's deliberate.
- **The sitemap uses a placeholder domain.** `public/sitemap.xml:3` has `https://trailhead.example/`. Replace it with your real origin.

## Worth considering

- **The guides page promises more than it shows:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `Routes graded from easy to strenuous.` No routes are listed. Listing them as text, each with its own page, might give readers and machines something to quote.
- **The home page has no text content:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `Walks across the Peak District`. It has a heading and a button but no description of the walks. A short intro might help.
- **Give each page its own title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' });`. Use `useHead` or `useSeoMeta` in each page.
- **Declare the site URL:** `nuxt.config.ts` has no site URL. Adding one would give canonicals and the sitemap a single source for the domain.
- **Admin is blocked in two ways:** `/admin` is in `robots.txt:2` and also noindexed at `pages/admin.vue:2`. This looks deliberate. Be aware that a crawler blocked by `robots.txt` never sees the `noindex`.

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-015 canonicals:** I need your real domain (`trailhead.example` looks like a placeholder). Once you give it, I'd expect the rule to be a Problem, since no page has a canonical.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** the real status codes for `/robots.txt` and the sitemap need a live check.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find the site.
- `/admin` is meant to stay private. I didn't count it against you.
- I sampled all three routes. There are no dynamic ones.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
